questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\int \dfrac{dx}{10^x + 10^{-x}}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Let $I = \int \dfrac{dx}{10^x + 10^{-x}}$

$I = \int \dfrac{10^x}{10^{2x} + 1} dx$

Let $10^x = t$

$10^x \ln 10 \, dx = dt \Rightarrow 10^x \, dx = \dfrac{dt}{\ln 10}$

$I = \dfrac{1}{\ln 10} \int \dfrac{dt}{t^2 + 1}$

$I = \dfrac{1}{\ln 10} \tan^{-1}(t) + c$

$I = \dfrac{1}{\ln 10} \tan^{-1}(10^x) + c$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{\ln 10}\tan^{-1}(10^x) + c$

questions.q:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let the function $y = (1 - \cos x)^{-1}$, where $x \neq 2n\pi$ and $n$ is an integer.

What is $\int y \, dx$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $y = (1 - \cos x)^{-1}$

$y = \dfrac{1}{1 - \cos x}$

Using the half-angle formula $1 - \cos x = 2 \sin^2(x/2)$

$y = \dfrac{1}{2 \sin^2(x/2)} = \dfrac{1}{2} \csc^2(x/2)$

Integrating with respect to $x$:

$\int y \, dx = \int \dfrac{1}{2} \csc^2(x/2) \, dx$

$\int y \, dx = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \dfrac{-\cot(x/2)}{1/2} \right) + c$

$\int y \, dx = -\cot(x/2) + c$

Answer: $-\cot(x/2) + c$

questions.q:
Let $\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}=\alpha(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\beta(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c$
What is the value of $\beta$ ?
questions.solution:
Given,
$\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}=\alpha(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\beta(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c\qquad ....(i)$
Let, $\quad \mathrm{I}=\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}\begin{aligned}
& =\int \frac{(\sqrt{x+1}+\sqrt{x-1}) d x}{(\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1})(\sqrt{x+1}+\sqrt{x-1})} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2} \int \sqrt{(x+1)} d x+\frac{1}{2} \int \sqrt{x-1} d x \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)}+\frac{\frac{1}{2}(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)}+c \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{3}(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\frac{1}{3}(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}=\frac{1}{3}(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\frac{1}{3}(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c \ldots(ii)
\end{aligned}$
From (i) and (ii) we get
$\beta=\frac{1}{3}$

Paragraph: Let $2 \int \frac{x^2-1}{\sqrt{x^2+1}} d x=\mathrm{U}(x) \mathrm{V}(x)-3 \ln \{\mathrm{U}(x)+\mathrm{V}(x)\}+c$
Question: What is $\mathrm{U}(x) \mathrm{V}(x)$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & I=2 \int \frac{x^2-1}{\sqrt{x^2+1}} d x=2 \int\left(\frac{x^2+1}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}\right) d x \\ & =2 \int\left(\sqrt{x^2+1}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}\right) d x \\ & =2\left[\frac{x}{2} \sqrt{x^2+1}+\frac{1}{2} \ln \left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)-2 \ln \left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)+c\right. \\ & =x \sqrt{x^2+1}+\ln \left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)-4 \ln \left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right) \\ & =x \sqrt{x^2+1}-3 \ln \left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)+c \\ & =U(x) \cdot V(x)-3 \ln \{U(x)+V(x)\}+c \\ & \therefore U(x)=x \text { and } V(x)=\sqrt{x^2+1}\end{aligned}\therefore \mathrm{U}(\mathrm{x}) \cdot \mathrm{V}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{x} \sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+1}=\sqrt{\mathrm{x}^4+\mathrm{x}^2}=\sqrt{\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{x}^4}$

questions.q:
Passage: Let $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{\sin\theta\,d\theta}{(2+\cos\theta)(3+4\cos\theta)}=A\ln|2+\cos\theta|+B\ln|3+4\cos\theta|$.

Question: What is the value of $A$ ?
questions.solution:
Let $I = \displaystyle\int\dfrac{\sin\theta\,d\theta}{(2+\cos\theta)(3+4\cos\theta)}$

Substitute $\cos\theta = t$, which gives $-\sin\theta\,d\theta = dt \Rightarrow \sin\theta\,d\theta = -dt$

$I = \displaystyle\int\dfrac{-dt}{(2+t)(3+4t)}$

Using partial fractions:

$\dfrac{-1}{(t+2)(4t+3)} = \dfrac{P}{t+2} + \dfrac{Q}{4t+3}$

$-1 = P(4t+3) + Q(t+2)$

Substituting $t = -2$, we get $-1 = P(-8+3) \Rightarrow P = \dfrac{1}{5}$

Substituting $t = -\dfrac{3}{4}$, we get $-1 = Q\left(-\dfrac{3}{4}+2\right) \Rightarrow Q = -\dfrac{4}{5}$

Therefore, the integral becomes:

$I = \displaystyle\int \left( \dfrac{1/5}{t+2} - \dfrac{4/5}{4t+3} \right) dt$

$I = \dfrac{1}{5}\ln|t+2| - \dfrac{4}{5} \cdot \dfrac{1}{4} \ln|4t+3| + C$

$I = \dfrac{1}{5}\ln|t+2| - \dfrac{1}{5}\ln|4t+3| + C$

Substituting back $t = \cos\theta$:

$I = \dfrac{1}{5}\ln|2+\cos\theta| - \dfrac{1}{5}\ln|3+4\cos\theta| + C$

Comparing this with $A\ln|2+\cos\theta| + B\ln|3+4\cos\theta|$, we get $A = \dfrac{1}{5}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{5}$

Question: What is $\left|\mathrm{U}^2(x)-\mathrm{V}^2(x)\right|$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & I=2 \int \frac{x^2-1}{\sqrt{x^2+1}} d x=2 \int\left(\frac{x^2+1}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}\right) d x \\ & =2 \int\left(\sqrt{x^2+1}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}\right) d x \\ & =2\left[\frac{x}{2} \sqrt{x^2+1}+\frac{1}{2} \ln \left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)-2 \ln \left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)+c\right. \\ & =x \sqrt{x^2+1}+\ln \left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)-4 \ln \left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right) \\ & =x \sqrt{x^2+1}-3 \ln \left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)+c \\ & =U(x) \cdot V(x)-3 \ln \{U(x)+V(x)\}+c \\ & \therefore U(x)=x \text { and } V(x)=\sqrt{x^2+1}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text { Now, }\left|\mathrm{U}^2(\mathrm{x})-\mathrm{V}^2(\mathrm{x})\right| \\ & =\left|\mathrm{x}^2-\left(\mathrm{x}^2+1\right)\right|=\left|\mathrm{x}^2-\mathrm{x}^2-1\right|=|-1|=1\end{aligned}$

Given that $\int \frac{3 \cos x+4 \sin x}{2 \cos x+5 \sin x} d x=\frac{\alpha x}{29}+\frac{\beta}{29} \ln |2 \cos x+5 \sin x|+c$
What is the value of $\beta$ ?
questions.solution:
Let,
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{I}=\int \frac{3 \cos x+4 \sin x}{2 \cos x+5 \sin x} d x \\
& 3 \cos x+4 \sin x=\mathrm{A}(2 \cos x+5 \sin x) \\
& +\mathrm{B}\left[\frac{d}{d x}(2 \cos x+5 \sin x)\right] \\
& 3 \cos x+4 \sin x=\mathrm{A}(2 \cos x+5 \sin x) \\
& +\mathrm{B}(-2 \sin x+5 \cos x)
\end{aligned}$
Comparing co-efficient of $\sin x$ and $\cos x\begin{aligned}
& 3=2 A+5 B \qquad ....(i)\\
& 4=5 A-2 B \qquad ....(ii)
\end{aligned}$
Solving (i) and (ii) then we get,
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{A}=\frac{26}{29}, \mathrm{~B}=\frac{7}{29} \\
& \mathrm{I}=\frac{\int \frac{26}{29}(2 \cos x+5 \sin x)+\frac{7}{29}(-2 \sin x+5 \cos x)}{2 \cos x+5 \sin x} d x \\
&=\int \frac{26}{29} d x+\frac{7}{29} \int \frac{(-2 \sin x+5 \cos x)}{2 \cos x+5 \sin x} d x \\
&=\frac{26}{29} x+\frac{7}{29} \text { In }(2 \cos x+5 \sin x)+c \\
& \alpha=26, \beta=7[\text { [on comparing] }
\end{aligned}\beta=7$

questions.q:
For the following two (02) items:
Let $u = \int e^x \cos x\, dx$ and $v = \int e^x \sin x\, dx$.

Consider the following:
I. $\dfrac{du}{dx} = -v$
II. $\dfrac{dv}{dx} = -u$
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Given $u = \int e^x \cos x\, dx$ and $v = \int e^x \sin x\, dx$.

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$, we get:
$\dfrac{du}{dx} = e^x \cos x$
$\dfrac{dv}{dx} = e^x \sin x$

Evaluating the integrals, we have:
$u = \dfrac{e^x}{2}(\cos x + \sin x) + C_1$
$v = \dfrac{e^x}{2}(\sin x - \cos x) + C_2$

Comparing the derivatives with $u$ and $v$, it is clear that:
$\dfrac{du}{dx} \neq -v$
$\dfrac{dv}{dx} \neq -u$

Therefore, neither statement I nor statement II is correct.

questions.q: If $\int \sqrt{1-\sin 2 x} d x=A \sin x+B \cos x+C$, where $0 \lt x \lt \frac{\pi}{4}$, then which one of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{I}=\int \sqrt{1-\sin ^2 x} d x, 0 \lt x \lt \frac{\pi}{4} \\
& =\int \sqrt{\sin ^2 x-2 \sin x \cos x+\cos ^2 x} d x \\
& =\int \sqrt{(\sin x-\cos x)^2} d x
\end{aligned}$
(i.e. $\sin x-\cos x \lt 0$ when $0 \lt x \lt \frac{\pi}{4}$ )
$\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \mathrm{I}=-\int(\sin x-\cos x) d x=\int(\cos x-\sin x) d x \\
& \mathrm{I}=\sin x-\cos x+c=\mathrm{A} \sin x+\mathrm{B} \cos x+\mathrm{c}
\end{aligned}$
Thus, $A+B=1-1=0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
For the following two (02) items:
Let $u = \int e^x \cos x\, dx$ and $v = \int e^x \sin x\, dx$.

What is $u + v$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $u = \int e^x \cos x\, dx$ and $v = \int e^x \sin x\, dx$

Adding $u$ and $v$:

$u + v = \int e^x (\cos x + \sin x)\, dx$

Using the standard integral $\int e^x (f(x) + f'(x))\, dx = e^x f(x)$, where $f(x) = \sin x$ and $f'(x) = \cos x$:

$u + v = e^x \sin x$

From the given expression for $v$, differentiating with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{d}{dx} \left( \int e^x \sin x\, dx \right) = e^x \sin x$

Therefore, $u + v = \dfrac{dv}{dx}$

Answer: $\dfrac{dv}{dx}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Passage: Let $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{\sin\theta\,d\theta}{(2+\cos\theta)(3+4\cos\theta)}=A\ln|2+\cos\theta|+B\ln|3+4\cos\theta|$.

Question: What is the value of $B$ ?
questions.solution:
Let $I = \displaystyle\int\dfrac{\sin\theta\,d\theta}{(2+\cos\theta)(3+4\cos\theta)}$.

Substitute $t = \cos\theta$, which gives $dt = -\sin\theta\,d\theta$.

The integral becomes:

$I = \displaystyle\int\dfrac{-dt}{(2+t)(3+4t)}$

Using partial fractions, we can write:

$\dfrac{-1}{(2+t)(3+4t)} = \dfrac{A'}{2+t} + \dfrac{B'}{3+4t}$

$-1 = A'(3+4t) + B'(2+t)$

Putting $t = -2$, we get $-1 = A'(3 - 8) \Rightarrow A' = \dfrac{1}{5}$.

Putting $t = -\dfrac{3}{4}$, we get $-1 = B'\left(2 - \dfrac{3}{4}\right) \Rightarrow -1 = B'\left(\dfrac{5}{4}\right) \Rightarrow B' = -\dfrac{4}{5}$.

So, the integral is:

$I = \displaystyle\int \left( \dfrac{1/5}{2+t} - \dfrac{4/5}{3+4t} \right) dt$

$I = \dfrac{1}{5}\ln|2+t| - \dfrac{4}{5} \times \dfrac{1}{4}\ln|3+4t| + C$

$I = \dfrac{1}{5}\ln|2+t| - \dfrac{1}{5}\ln|3+4t| + C$

Substituting back $t = \cos\theta$:

$I = \dfrac{1}{5}\ln|2+\cos\theta| - \dfrac{1}{5}\ln|3+4\cos\theta| + C$

Comparing this with the given expression $A\ln|2+\cos\theta| + B\ln|3+4\cos\theta|$, we get:

$B = -\dfrac{1}{5}$

Answer: $-\dfrac{1}{5}$

questions.q:
Let $\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}=\alpha(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\beta(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c$
What is the value of $\alpha$ ?
questions.solution:
Given,
$\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}=\alpha(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\beta(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c\qquad ....(i)$
Let, $\quad \mathrm{I}=\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}\begin{aligned}
& =\int \frac{(\sqrt{x+1}+\sqrt{x-1}) d x}{(\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1})(\sqrt{x+1}+\sqrt{x-1})} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2} \int \sqrt{(x+1)} d x+\frac{1}{2} \int \sqrt{x-1} d x \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)}+\frac{\frac{1}{2}(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)}+c \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{3}(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\frac{1}{3}(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}=\frac{1}{3}(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\frac{1}{3}(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c \ldots(ii)
\end{aligned}$
From (i) and (ii) we get
$\alpha=\frac{1}{3}$

questions.q: What is $\int \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{x}\left(\mathrm{x}^7+1\right)}$ equal to?

Then $\int \frac{x^6 d x}{x^7\left(x^7+1\right)}=\frac{1}{7} \int \frac{d t}{t(t+1)}\begin{aligned}

\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
Let $f(\mathrm{x})$ be an indefinite integral of $\sin ^2 \mathrm{x}$. Consider the following statements :
Statement 1 : The function $f(\mathrm{x})$ satisfies $f(\mathrm{x}+\pi)=f(\mathrm{x})$ for all real x .
Statement $2: \sin ^2(x+\pi)=\sin ^2 x$ for all real $x$.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both the statements are true and Statement 2 is the correct explanation of Statement 1
Both the statements are true but Statement 2 is not the correct explanation of Statement 1
Statement 1 is true but Statement 2 is false
Statement 1 is false but Statement 2 is false
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & f(x)=\int \sin ^2 x \cdot d x=\int \frac{1-\cos 2 x}{2} \cdot d x \\ & =\frac{1}{2} x-\frac{\sin 2 x}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2}+c=\frac{1}{2} x-\frac{1}{4} \sin 2 x+c\end{aligned}$
(i)
$\begin{aligned}
& f(\pi+x)=\frac{1}{2}(\pi+x)-\frac{1}{4} \sin 2(\pi+x) \\
& =\frac{1}{2} \pi+\frac{1}{2} x-\frac{1}{2} \sin (2 \pi+2 x)+c \\
& =\frac{x}{2}-\frac{1}{2} \sin 2 x+c=f(x)
\end{aligned}$
So, statement 1 is true.
(ii)
$\begin{aligned}
& \sin ^2(\pi+x)=\sin ^2 x \\
& (-\sin x)^2=\sin ^2 x \\
& \Rightarrow \sin ^2 x=\sin ^2 x
\end{aligned}$
So, statement 2 is true

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\int \frac{x^4-1}{x^2 \sqrt{x^4+x^2+1}} d x$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Take option (1)
$I_1=\sqrt{\frac{x^4+x^3+1}{x}}+C\begin{aligned}
\frac{d I_1}{d x} & =\frac{d}{d x}\left[\left(x^3+x^2+x^{-1}\right)^{1 / 2}+C\right] \\
\frac{d I_2}{d x} & =\frac{1}{2}\left(x^3+x^2+x^{-1}\right)^{-1 / 2}\left(3 x^2+2 x-x^{-2}\right) \\
& =\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{3 x^2+2 x-\frac{1}{x^2}}{\sqrt{x^3+x^2+\frac{1}{x}}}\right] \\
\frac{d I_2}{d x} & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{3 x^4+2 x^3-1}{\frac{x^2}{\sqrt{x}} \sqrt{x^4+x^3+1}}\right]
\end{aligned}$
Take option (b) :
$\begin{aligned}
I_2 & =\sqrt{x^4+2-\frac{1}{x^2}}+C \\
\frac{d I_2}{d x} & =\frac{1}{2}\left[x^4+2-x^{-2}\right]^{-1 / 2}\left[4 x^3+0+2 x^{-3}\right] \\
& =\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{4 x^3+\frac{2}{x^3}}{\sqrt{x^4+2-\frac{1}{x^2}}}\right]=\frac{2 x^6+1}{\frac{x^3}{x} \sqrt{x^6+2 x^2-1}} \\
\frac{d I_2}{d x} & =\frac{2 x^6+1}{x^2 \sqrt{x^6+2 x-1}}
\end{aligned}$
Take option (3) :
$\begin{aligned}
& I_3=\sqrt{x^2+x^{-2}+1}+C \\
& \frac{d I_3}{d x}=\frac{1}{2}\left[x^2+x^{-2}+1\right]^{-1 / 2}\left[2 x-2 x^{-3}+0\right] \\
& =\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{2 x-\frac{2}{x^3}}{\sqrt{x^2+\frac{1}{x^2}+1}}\right]=\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{2\left(x^4-1\right)}{x^3 \sqrt{\frac{x^4+1+x^2}{x^2}}}\right] \\
& \frac{d I_3}{d x}=\frac{x^4-1}{x^2 \sqrt{x^4+x^2+1}}
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Option (3) is correct answer.

questions.q: If $I_1=\int \frac{e^x d x}{e^x+e^{-x}}$ and $I_2=\int \frac{d x}{e^{2 x}+1}$, then what is $I_1+I_2$ equal to?

questions.q: What is $\int e^{\sin x} \frac{x \cos ^3 x-\sin x}{\cos ^2 x} d x$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Let us differentiate all the options one by one to get the expression in the question whose integral is to be found.
Here $x e^{\sin x}$ is the common term in all the options. So, let us differentiate it first.
$\begin{aligned}
& \text { Let } l=x e^{\sin x} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{d l}{d x}=e^{\sin x}[x \cos x+1] \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{d l}{d x}=\frac{e^{\sin x}}{\cos ^2 x}\left[x \cos ^3 x+\cos ^2 x\right]
\end{aligned}$
Let $m=\sec x e^{\sin x}\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \frac{d m}{d x}=\sec x e^{\sin x} \cdot \cos x+e^{\sin x} \sec x \tan x \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{d m}{d x}=e^{\sin x}\left[1+\frac{\sin x}{\cos ^2 x}\right] \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{d m}{d x}=\frac{e^{\sin x}}{\cos ^2 x}\left[\cos ^2 x+\sin x\right]
\end{aligned}$
Differentiation of option (a) is
$\begin{aligned}
& =\frac{e^{\sin x}}{\cos ^2 x}\left[x \cos ^3 x+\cos ^2 x+\cos ^2 x+\sin x\right] \\
& =\frac{e^{\sin x}}{\cos ^2 x}\left[x \cos ^3 x+2 \cos ^2 x+\sin x\right]
\end{aligned}$
Differentiation of option (b) is
$\begin{aligned}
& =\frac{e^{\sin x}}{\cos ^2 x}\left[x \cos ^3 x+\cos ^2 x-\cos ^2 x-\sin x\right] \\
& =\frac{e^{\sin x}}{\cos ^2 x}\left[x \cos ^3 x-\sin x\right]
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Option (2) is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the function $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=(\mathrm{x}-1)^2(\mathrm{x}+1)(\mathrm{x}-2)^3$.
Let $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ be twice differentiable functions on $[0,2]$ satisfying $\mathrm{f}^{\prime \prime}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{g}^{\prime \prime}(\mathrm{x}), \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(1)=4, \mathrm{~g}^{\prime}(1)=6, f(2)=3$ and $g(2)=9$. Then what is $f(x)-g(x)$ at $x=4$ equal to ?
questions.solution:
$f^{\prime \prime}(x)=g^{\prime \prime}(x)$
integrate b|s w.r.t. (x)
$f^{\prime}(x)+C_1=g^{\prime}(x)+C_2$  ...(1)
Putting $x=1\begin{aligned}
& f^{\prime}(1)+C_1=g^{\prime}(1)+C_2 \\
& \Rightarrow C_1-C_2=g^{\prime}(1)-f^{\prime}(1) \\
& \Rightarrow C_1-C_2=6-4=2
\end{aligned}$
again integrating equation (1)
$f(x)+C_1 x+a_1=g(x)+C_2 x+a_2$  ...(3)
Putting $x=2\begin{aligned}
& f(2)+C_1 \times 2+a_1=g(2)+2 C_2+a_2 \\
& \Rightarrow a_1-a_2=g(2)+2 C_2-2 C_1-f(2) \\
& \quad=9-3-2\left(C_1-C_2\right) \\
& \quad=6-2 \times 2=2 \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}_1-\mathrm{a}_2=2
\end{aligned}$
Rearranging equation (3) again, we get
$f(x)-g(x)=-x\left(C_1-C_2\right)-\left(a_1-a_2\right)$
Putting $x=4$, we get
$\begin{aligned}
{[f(x)-g(x)]_{x=4} } & =-4\left(C_1-C_2\right)-\left(a_1-a_2\right) \\
& =-4 \times(2)-2 \\
{[f(x)-g(x)]_{x=4} } & =-10
\end{aligned}$

The integral $\int \frac{d x}{a \cos x+b \sin x}$ is of the form $\frac{1}{r} \operatorname{In}\left[\tan \left(\frac{x+\alpha}{2}\right)\right]$.
What is $r$ equal to?

Given that, $\int \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{a} \cos \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{b} \sin \mathrm{x}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{r}} \ln \left[\tan \left(\frac{\mathrm{x}+\alpha}{2}\right)\right]$
Let $\mathrm{a}=\mathrm{r} \sin \alpha, \mathrm{b}=\mathrm{r} \cos \alpha\begin{aligned}
& \int \frac{d x}{r \sin \alpha \cos x+r \cos \alpha \sin x}=\frac{1}{r} \int \frac{1}{\sin (x+\alpha)} \\

\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& a=r \sin \alpha \Rightarrow a^2=r^2 \sin ^2 \alpha ...(i)\\
& b=r \cos \alpha \Rightarrow b^2=r^2 \cos ^2 \alpha...(ii)
\end{aligned}$
Adding (i) and (ii), we get
$\Rightarrow \quad \begin{aligned}
\mathrm{r}^2 & =\mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{b}^2 \\
\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{r} & =\sqrt{\mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{b}^2} .
\end{aligned}$

& =\ln \left[\frac{x}{\sqrt{a^2}}+\sqrt{1+\frac{x^2}{a^2}}\right]+c \\
& =\ln \left[\frac{x}{a}+\frac{\sqrt{a^2+x^2}}{a}\right]+c \\
& =\ln \left[\frac{x+\sqrt{x^2+a^2}}{a}\right]+c
\end{aligned}\therefore \quad$ Option (A) is correct.

Consider $\int x \tan ^{-1} x d x=\mathrm{A}\left(x^2+1\right) \tan ^{-1} x+\mathrm{B} x+\mathrm{C}$, where C is the constant of integration.
What is the value of A ?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \int x \cdot \tan ^{-1} x d x=\mathrm{A}\left(x^2+1\right) \tan ^{-1} x+\mathrm{B} x+\mathrm{C} \\ & \text {Let } \mathrm{I}=\int x \cdot \tan ^{-1} x d x \\ &=\tan ^{-1} x \cdot\left(\frac{x^2}{2}\right)-\int \frac{1}{1+x^2} \cdot \frac{x^2}{2} d x \\ &=\frac{x^2}{2} \cdot \tan ^{-1} x-\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{x^2}{1+x^2} d x \\ &=\frac{x^2}{2} \cdot \tan ^{-1} x-\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{\left(1+x^2\right)-1}{1+x^2} d x \\ &=\frac{x^2}{2} \cdot \tan ^{-1} x-\frac{1}{2}\left[\int 1 d x-\int \frac{1}{1+x^2} d x\right] \\ &=\frac{x^2}{2} \cdot \tan ^{-1} x-\frac{1}{2}\left[x-\tan ^{-1} x\right]+\mathrm{C} \\ &=\frac{x^2}{2} \cdot \tan ^{-1} x-\frac{1}{2} x+\frac{1}{2} \tan ^{-1} x+\mathrm{C} \\ &=\left(\frac{x^2+1}{2}\right) \tan ^{-1} x-\frac{x}{2}+\mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$
Value of $\mathrm{A}=\frac{1}{2}$

questions.q: $\int(\operatorname{In} x)^{-1} d x-\int(\operatorname{In} x)^{-2} d x$ is equal to
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \int(\ln x)^{-1} d x-\int(\ln x)^{-2} d x \\ & =\int\left[\frac{1}{\ln x}-\frac{1}{(\ln x)^2}\right] d x\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text { Put } \ell \mathrm{n} \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{t} \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{t}} \\ & \mathrm{dx}=\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{t}} . \mathrm{dt} .\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \therefore \int\left[\frac{1}{\ln \mathrm{x}}-\frac{1}{(\ln \mathrm{x})^2}\right] \mathrm{dx}=\int\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}^2}\right) \cdot \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{t}} \cdot \mathrm{dt} \\ & =\int \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{t}} \cdot\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}^2}\right) \cdot \mathrm{dt}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\int \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{t}} \cdot\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}^2}\right) \cdot \mathrm{dt} \\ & =\frac{\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{t}}}{\mathrm{t}}+\mathrm{c}=\frac{\mathrm{x}}{\ln \mathrm{x}}+\mathrm{c}\end{aligned}=x(\ln x)^{-1}+c$

questions.q:
What is $\int \sqrt{x} e^{\sqrt{x}} d x$ equal to?
where $c$ is a constant of integration.
questions.solution:
$\int \sqrt{x} e^{\sqrt{x}} d x$
Put $\sqrt{x}=u\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x}}=d u \\ & \therefore d x=2 \sqrt{x} d u \\ &= \int u^2 e^u d u \times 2 \\ &= 2\left[u^2 \int e^u d u-\int 2 u e^u d u\right] \\ &= 2\left[u^2 \cdot e^u-2\left\{e^u \cdot u-e^u\right\}\right] \\ &= 2 u^2 e^u-4 u e^u+4 e^u \\ &= 2 x e^{\sqrt{x}}-4 \sqrt{x} e^{\sqrt{x}}+4 e^{\sqrt{x}} \\ &= 2 e^{\sqrt{x}}(x-2 \sqrt{x}+2)\end{aligned}$
